thread:
incident-bot: :warning: Incident opened — elevated 5xx and high tail latency observed in eu-central-1 affecting Hosted API frontends and several Dedicated pools. Detection: 2026-03-17T12:34:00Z. Likely upstream: AWS STS errors + observability ingest throttling. Pager: @alex

alex: I'm oncall, starting triage. creating bridge and collecting impact. @mia please take auth traces and STS time-series.

mia: on it. lots of 500/503 from sts.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com between 12:33-12:36Z. token exchange errors causing auth failures -> frontend 5xx. also seeing our log vendor return 429 for eu-central-1 ingest, backlog building.

jordan: rerouting new traffic away from eu-central-1 to reduce load. shifting 65% to eu-west-1 now.

jordan: applied routing change: 
```
redwoodctl routing set --region eu-central-1 --fallback eu-west-1 --new-weight 65
```

alex: good. @mia can we throttle STS retries and prefer cached creds? want to avoid amplifying failures.

mia: implemented aggressive local cache for session tokens with short TTLs and disabled eager refresh. reduced retry concurrency/backoff to exponential. also added fast-path for requests with valid tokens.

norma: customer impact summary for status: error rate peaked ~7% on some Hosted frontends; Dedicated pools serving EU tenants saw latency spikes and retries. Notifying CS for high-touch customers.

ram: CS: two customers reported 5xxs (org fastshop, org docwrite). I've acknowledged and shared the bridge. Will push status update to them.

jordan: scaling additional Dedicated capacity in eu-west-1 to absorb diverted traffic.

jordan: infra command: 
```
infractl scale --cluster dedicated-eu-west-1 --delta +3
```

mia: quick checks for bridge joiners: 
```
curl -sS https://api.eu-central-1.redwood.ai/health | jq .
kubectl -n infra get pods -l region=eu-central-1 -o wide
```

lina: PM note — cause looks like a regional cascade: STS token errors + observability ingress rate-limiting. routing and cache mitigations in flight. next: confirm AWS STS stability or prepare prolonged failover plan.

alex: I'll hold primary until 12:50 UTC then hand to @mia. bridge: https://zoom.example/incident-1789601234 (created). severity P2 for now.

incident-bot: Bridge created by alex. severity=P2. will update if customer impact worsens.

mia: contacted log vendor (logs-eu) — they confirmed throttling on eu-central intake and are rerouting part of their ingest to eu-west-1. that explains telemetry gaps and backlog. plausible sequence: STS errors -> retries -> increased telemetry + token churn -> vendor throttle -> more retries.

norma: draft status page copy: "We are investigating elevated errors and latency impacting EU (eu-central-1). Traffic is being routed to eu-west-1 and mitigations are applied. Some customers may see 5xx errors or increased latency. Updates in 30 minutes."

ram: posted proactive note to affected customers with bridge link and status draft.

jordan: eu-west-1 scale-up finished, new Dedicated nodes healthy and accepting traffic. monitoring error rate now.

mia: Hosted API error-rate in eu-central-1 started trending down after routing change; intermittent STS 5xxs persist for token exchanges. keeping cached token TTL and reduced retry concurrency until STS stable.

alex: next steps: monitor for 30-60m, confirm customers recovery, keep clear handoffs. if error rate >3% for prolonged period or customer escalations increase, escalate to P1 and loop in platform ENG leads.

lina: post-incident follow-ups: timeline, root cause hypothesis (AWS STS + observability ingress throttle), and mitigation checklist (regional token caching, smarter retry caps, multi-region vendor failover testing).

incident-bot: Incident update logged. last_event=2026-03-17T12:49:09Z

alex: handing primary to @mia now. Mia please capture timeline notes for postmortem.

mia: taking over. saving traces and artifacts to /incidents/1789601234/artifacts. compiling timestamps and STS call traces.

ram: CS will follow up with affected customers once we confirm recovery. :white_check_mark:

alex: thanks team, nice coordination. :rocket:
